experiment: 1H-15N TROSY and TRACT (rotational correlation times) of [2H,15N] CheA; field strength not stated
other_conditions: tumbling: P1 domain ~30 ns, P2 domain ~15 ns, versus 68 ns expected from the size of CheA; related structures: none; temperature, pH and buffer of the TRACT measurement are not stated
dynamics_type: inter-domain flexibility (P1 and P2 domains tumble independently through flexible linkers)
author_claim: The P1 and P2 domains of full-length CheA tumble much faster than the whole CheA, so they are structurally isolated from the P3-P5 domains by flexible linkers.
anchor: These values are remarkably smaller than those expected from the size of CheA (68 ns), suggesting that the P1 and P2 domains are structurally isolated from the other domains by flexible linkers
locator: Results, first section (TRACT); Supplementary Fig. S2
caveat_note: Correlation times are overall domain tumbling values, not internal dynamics rates. TRACT conditions (temperature, pH, buffer, field) are not given in the main text, so they are left empty. The entry sequence covers only the P1 region (residues 1-134), so this is the same protein in a full-length construct. Detection window is ns tumbling only.

experiment: 1H-13C HMQC titration of methyl-labeled P1 domain of segmentally labeled CheA with non-labeled CheY, I5 and M3 methyl resonances; MCMC fit of McConnell-equation simulations; field strength not stated
ligand_or_partner: non-labeled CheY, titrated; 100 μM CheA; 0.1 mM CheY favors the P1-CheY bound state and 0.9 mM CheY favors the doubly-bound state
construct_or_mutation: full-length E. coli CheA, segmentally labeled [u-2H, Ileδ1-13CH3, Metε-13CH3, Alaβ-13CH3]-P1/[2H]-P2–5 CheA; wild-type CheY
other_conditions: related structures: 2LP4 (E. coli isolated P1-P2-CheY model), 3KYJ (R. sphaeroides P1-CheY), 1I5N (isolated P1 domain); fixed in fits: association rates 2 × 10^8 M−1 s−1, 10,000 s−1 and 10^7 M−1 s−1, and 1H and 13C transverse relaxation rates at 303 K of 45 s−1 and 12 s−1 (free state) and 60 s−1 and 15 s−1 (bound states); regime (authors): fast exchange regimes; isolated P1 domain Kd = 900 μM (700-1,100 μM) for comparison; buffer and pH of the HMQC titration are not stated
dynamics_type: ligand-coupled domain rearrangement; exchange among free, P1-CheY unbound, P1-CheY bound and doubly-bound states
timescale: association rates set to 2 × 10^8 M−1 s−1, 10,000 s−1 and 10^7 M−1 s−1 (fixed constants, fast exchange) (four-state MCMC fit to I5 1H/13C shifts)
population: apparent Kd of the P1-CheY bound state = 1.6 μM (0.1–2 μM) from I5 1H shifts; apparent Kd of the doubly-bound state = 1,000 μM from I5 13C shifts; P2 domain Kd = 0.5 μM (0.1 ~ 2 μM), >80% of P2 bound at a stoichiometric amount of CheY
author_claim: In the full-length CheA-CheY complex the P1 domain binds CheY with a micromolar apparent affinity, which the isolated P1 domain does not show, so the complex exchanges among states with different domain arrangements.
anchor: The apparent dissociation constants of the P1-CheY bound state and the doubly-bound state are 1.6 μM and 1,000 μM, respectively, as calculated from the resonances from I5 of CheA
locator: Results, first section; Fig. 1d-g, Fig. 5a; conditions: Methods, Simulations and Fig. 1 legend
caveat_note: The exchange is fast and only population-weighted averaged shifts are observed, so no state-specific spectra or microscopic rate constants are measured. Association rates were fixed rather than fitted. The P1-CheY unbound state is inferred indirectly from the doubly-bound state. Buffer and pH of the HMQC titration are not stated, and the Tris pH 7.5 conditions are given for the 1H-15N TROSY titrations. Doubly-bound Kd and the mapping of non-linear shifts to states depend on the four-state model.

experiment: 1H-13C HMQC titration of methyl-labeled P1 domain of segmentally labeled CheA with non-labeled CheY at 283 K versus 303 K, I5 and M3 methyl resonances; MCMC fit of McConnell-equation simulations; field strength not stated
construct_or_mutation: full-length E. coli CheA, segmentally labeled [u-2H, Ileδ1-13CH3, Metε-13CH3, Alaβ-13CH3]-P1/[2H]-P2–5 CheA; wild-type CheY
other_conditions: comparison with 303 K data; related structures: none; fixed in fits: 1H and 13C transverse relaxation rates at 283 K of 70 s−1 and 40 s−1 (free state) and 100 s−1 and 60 s−1 (bound states); association rates 2 × 10^8 M−1 s−1, 10,000 s−1 and 10^7 M−1 s−1; regime (authors): exchange rates faster than the NMR timescale; buffer and pH of the HMQC titration are not stated
dynamics_type: temperature-dependent population shift between P1-CheY unbound and bound states
timescale: exchange rates = >1,000 s−1 (fast exchange, qualitative lower bound); association rates fixed at 2 × 10^8 M−1 s−1, 10,000 s−1 and 10^7 M−1 s−1 (four-state MCMC fit of I5 shifts at 283 K and 303 K)
population: at 283 K the equilibrium is shifted toward the P1-CheY unbound state and the doubly-bound state population is larger than at 303 K (koff1/kon1 at 283 K larger than at 303 K); enthalpy change of the unbound-to-bound equilibrium (van't Hoff, 283 and 303 K) ~30 kJ/mol (10 ~ 40 kJ/mol); simulated ~30% change in phosphorylated CheY
author_claim: The CheA-CheY complex exchanges rapidly between the P1-CheY bound and unbound states, and warming shifts the equilibrium toward the P1-CheY bound state that favors phosphotransfer, which can act as the thermosensor of warm-seeking thermotaxis.
anchor: These results suggested that the CheA-CheY complex exists in equilibrium between the P1-CheY bound state and the P1-CheY unbound state, with exchange rates faster than the NMR timescale (>1,000 s −1 )
locator: Results, section 'Equilibrium shifts toward the P1-CheY bound state with increasing temperature'; Figs 2-5; Discussion (van't Hoff); conditions: Methods, Simulations
caveat_note: Only a lower bound on the exchange rate is obtained, and the fits assume fixed association rates and relaxation rates. Only two temperatures were compared, so the enthalpy has a wide range. The link to thermotaxis relies on a simulated signaling model. The 283 K and 303 K shifts could also reflect temperature-dependent chemical shifts of the end states, although the authors limited those differences (0.01 and 0.05 ppm) in the fit. Buffer and pH of the HMQC titration are not stated.
